messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Possible cross-tenant response exposure detected for a dedicated pool serving Customer 912 (AcmeApps). Severity: P1. Pattern: overlapping routing prefixes observed in pool-dedicated-7. Please ack and follow on-call runbook. https://infra.internal/incidents/1815045560

maria: Acked. I’m on it. Pulling logs from pool-dedicated-7 and starting triage.

ajay: On-call takeover in 5. @maria handoff?

maria: Quick sketch — appears some requests for AcmeApps (tenant_id: cust-912) returned content that included another tenant’s prompt fragments. Early hypothesis: control plane route update accidentally published a superset prefix to the shared router, causing tenant prefix collision.

lee: If true, scope is dedicated pool routing table only? Any VPC customers impacted?

maria: Initial checks: only pool-dedicated-7, which hosts a mix of dedicated and reserved VPC binds for enterprise customers. VPC routing isolates at the vnic level, but our pool routing layer had a stale prefix entry for cust-912 that overlapped cust-834.

priya: Paging security. @sam_security please join — customer data exposure possible.
sam_security: Joining. Thanks. Can we capture sample request/response pairs (redacted) and timestamp ranges? Need to determine if sensitive tokens leaked.

maria: Captured sample and redacted locally. Running quick audit query:
```
SELECT request_id, tenant_id, route_prefix, response_snippet
FROM routing_logs
WHERE pool = 'pool-dedicated-7'
  AND ts >= 1615042000
  AND ts <= 1615045400
  AND response_snippet LIKE '%customer-specific-keyword%';
```

ajay: Results?

maria: Query returned 6 matches. Two unique request_ids show response_snippet containing fragments that match another tenant’s prompt id. No full secrets seen, but leakage of PII-like strings is possible.

ops-bot: Automated action: created incident ticket INC-2026-1815045560, notified account team.

lee: Immediate mitigation options: (1) Evacuate cust-912 off pool-dedicated-7 to fallback isolated pool (cold-swap) (2) Patch router to remove overlapping prefix and restart route daemon (3) Invalidate per-tenant KV cache entries. Which to do first?

maria: Do 1 + 3 concurrently. Evac first to stop live exposure. Then invalidate caches. Patching router and rolling reconfigure after isolation.

priya: I’ll coordinate evacuation with networking. Steps: drain pool node set A, create dedicated nodes under pool-isolated-3, update customer binding to isolated nodes, confirm connectivity to VPC.

ajay: I’m taking live runbook exec. Run commands I’ll run:
```
# mark tenant 912 for evacuation
redwoodctl tenant evict --tenant cust-912 --from-pool pool-dedicated-7 --to-pool pool-isolated-3 --reason "routing overlap"
# invalidate KV cache
redwoodctl cache invalidate --tenant cust-912 --scope kv
```

maria: Executed eviction command, started cache invalidation. Observed 200/200 active sessions migrated within ~40s.

sam_security: Good. Now rotate any ephemeral keys that may have been cached and collect copy of the redacted samples for legal/sre. Also notify SRE leads to freeze any automated route publishes to that pool.

lee: Freeze enacted via infra-protect: `route-publish-lock pool-dedicated-7 --enable`

priya: Noted. Customer success is being looped in. I’m drafting a light initial message: "We detected anomalous routing behavior affecting a dedicated pool; we are isolating your traffic and conducting an audit. No confirmed secret exfiltration at this time. We will follow up with findings." Thoughts? Keep it conservative.

ajay: Sounds good. Keep legal and account-team in the loop.

maria: Running deeper audit now for cross-tenant routing update history:
```
SELECT * FROM route_events WHERE pool='pool-dedicated-7' AND ts >= 1615038000 ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 50;
```

maria: Found a route-update from deploy-bot at ts=1615041822 that included a merged prefix list — human error during a manual merge to accommodate a new enterprise onboarding, the route validation step skipped because of a transient validation service outage.

sam_security: That’s a clear root cause candidate. We need to preserve timeline and config diffs. Also gather who executed the merge.

ops-bot: Audit artifact attached to incident ticket: /incidents/1815045560/artifacts/route-diff-1615041822.diff

priya: Customer update sent (CS queued). Engineering mitigation in progress.

ajay: Any residual traffic hitting old route?

maria: After eviction, near-zero. I see two retries from older clients which were redirected and failed gracefully. Last_message at 1615047000 shows no further overlap matches.

sam_security: Action items for now:
- Forensic capture of sample payloads (redacted) — sam_security
- Rotate ephemeral keys and check KMS logs — infra-security
- Postmortem & timeline — engineering + SRE
- Customer notification and CC legal — CS + legal

lee: Also propose an immediate changelist to harden route validation: prevent merge if validation service unreachable plus a dry-run acceptance gate. I’ll draft CL.

maria: Agree. I’ll follow up with logs and attach to ticket. Going to start a short RCA doc and link it.

priya: Thanks all. Handing off to @ajay for 2nd shift. I’ll remain on the loop for CS comms.

ajay: Taking over monitoring. If anything new shows up ping me directly.

ops-bot: Incident status: mitigation: in-progress -> containment achieved at 1615046900. No new exposures detected after evacuation.

maria: Adding final notes: root cause: manual route merge during validation outage led to overlapping prefixes published to pool-dedicated-7 causing routing ambiguity and cache reuse across two tenant prefixes. Blast radius limited to pool-dedicated-7.

sam_security: We will run retrospective and coordinate disclosure scope with legal. Preliminary severity remains P1 until postmortem.

lee: Thanks team. Follow-ups tracked in INC-2026-1815045560. Will schedule postmortem tomorrow at 09:00 PT.

priya: Closing pager, leaving incident open for RCA. :white_check_mark:

ajay: Acknowledged.

incident-bot: Incident update: status=contained, severity=P1 -> P2 (for RCA). Next: postmortem scheduled.
